points.why: Names both the reporting lag and the delivery lag in an order-correction loop and says this delay alone makes it overshoot and undershoot.
Says the pattern occurs regardless of who runs the process and that a new buyer would inherit the same cycle.
Explains that doubling on a late shortage signal arrives after the need has passed and makes the oscillation stronger.
Recommends live dispensing data and more frequent review to cut delays, and offers to test the current versus proposed policy against past data before acting.

pitfalls.why: Advises against replacing the buyer and suggests checking their decisions against the data first.
Explicitly rejects the order-double rule as amplifying swings.
